answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to emit a regular, verifiable pulse of useful work: small, independently checkable tasks whose results are signed and timestamped. An identity that has completed a long voyage of such pulses accumulates a costly, unforgeable history, while a fresh swarm of clones starts with nothing. Because the meadow of available work is rate-limited per identity and each pulse consumes real compute, creating thousands of fake agents costs thousands of times more than running one honest agent, and the market simply prices the clones out.
